standard.title: Tables of Values and Graphing
standard.description: generate tables of values from visually growing patterns or the rule of a function; describe and plot these relationships on the Cartesian plane
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can plot points in all four quadrants of the Cartesian plane (from AC9M6SP02). Students can write rules for growing patterns (from AC9M6A01, AC9M6A03).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students generate tables of values from growing patterns or function rules, plot the relationships on the Cartesian plane, and describe the resulting graph.

nodes.label: Generating tables of values from patterns
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students identify the rule in a visually growing pattern and use it to generate a table of values.
nodes.minimum_width: Given a visual growing pattern, complete a table of values for the first 5 terms.
nodes.typical_width: Identify the rule in words and algebraic notation; use the rule to generate values including for non-consecutive terms.
wider: Investigate growing patterns using physical materials (tiles, blocks) and connect the physical growth to the algebraic rule.
Compare two growing patterns — which grows faster? How can you tell from the table?

response_modes.reason: Students who only see numerical patterns without visual context often generate tables mechanically without understanding the rule. Visual pattern contexts anchor the algebraic structure.

success_criteria: Correctly generates a table of values from a growing pattern.
Identifies the rule that generates the values.
Can find the value for a term not shown in the original pattern.

nodes.label: Generating tables from function rules
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students generate a table of ordered pairs from a given function rule and identify the relationship between input and output values.
nodes.minimum_width: Given a simple function rule (e.g. y = 2x + 1), generate a table of at least 5 ordered pairs.
nodes.typical_width: Generate tables from various linear function rules; describe the pattern in the output values; identify the effect of changing the rule.
wider: Use a function machine or spreadsheet to generate tables for multiple rules and compare outputs side by side.
Investigate what happens to the table when the rule changes: how does doubling the coefficient change the values?

response_modes.reason: Systematic generation of ordered pairs requires procedural care that students need to practise before plotting. Errors in the table cascade into errors in the graph.

nodes.hinge_reason: Errors in the table of ordered pairs cascade directly into Node 3 — incorrectly generated pairs produce a graph that doesn't represent the function rule, meaning students cannot see or describe the relationship they were supposed to plot.
success_criteria: Correctly generates a table of ordered pairs from a given function rule.
Labels the table with input (x) and output (y) columns.
Does not substitute the same value for both x and y.

nodes.label: Plotting and describing relationships on the Cartesian plane
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students plot ordered pairs from a table of values on the Cartesian plane and describe the resulting relationship.
nodes.minimum_width: Plot a set of ordered pairs from a table and connect them; describe whether the relationship is linear.
nodes.typical_width: Plot and describe relationships for several linear rules; identify that linear functions produce straight lines; describe slope informally.
wider: Compare two functions plotted on the same axes — identify what differs (steepness, y-intercept) and connect to the rule.
Investigate the graphical representation of a non-linear function (e.g. y = x²) from a table — contrast with linear.

response_modes.reason: Plotting connects the table of values, the function rule, and the Cartesian plane simultaneously. Describing the resulting graph requires coordinating all three representations.

success_criteria: Correctly plots ordered pairs from a table on the Cartesian plane.
Draws a line through plotted points for a linear relationship.
Describes the relationship shown in the graph using appropriate language.
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Comparing two functions on the same axes and connecting visual differences to rule differences (steepness, intercept) is genuinely rich — advancing students can begin to reason about what the rule parameters control.
